territorial_scope.description: Governs exports and reexports from the United States of controlled items to validated end users in listed destinations, and names approved end users in Supplement No. 7 to part 748.

evidence.quote: Data Center VEU Authorizations may be used for any destination for which a license is required for ECCN 3A090, 4A090 items

summary.short: Amends the Export Administration Regulations to add a Data Center Validated End User (VEU) authorization allowing exports and reexports of controlled items for data centers to preapproved end users in destinations requiring a license, excluding D:5 countries and 600 series items. Effective 2 October 2024.
summary.long: The rule adds a Data Center Validated End User (VEU) Authorization to the Export Administration Regulations, effective 2 October 2024, alongside the existing General VEU Authorization for China and India. It permits exports and reexports of Commerce Control List items that require a license to destinations other than Country Group D:5 (excluding 600 series items) for use in data centers, to end users approved by the End-User Review Committee and listed in Supplement No. 7 to part 748. Applicants submit an advisory opinion request with the information in Supplement No. 8, including security and information-security plans, a supply-chain risk plan and a list of current and potential customers; the committee's evaluation includes whether the host country has given assurances on safe and secure use. Exporters must obtain end-use certifications before a first export. Reexporters and Data Center VEU end users file semiannual reports with BIS, and records are subject to review and on-site inspection. Items may be used at the end user's own facility in an authorized destination, consumed, or reexported only as BIS authorizes; in-country transfers are restricted, and part 744 activities are barred. Authorizations may be revised, suspended or revoked.

definitions.term: Eligible items for Data Center VEU Authorizations

evidence.quote: Eligible items for Data Center VEU Authorizations are all those items on the Commerce Control List, that require a license to the destination excluding ‘‘600 series’’ items, and are necessary for a data center.

Data Center VEU Authorizations may be used for any destination for which a license is required for ECCN 3A090, 4A090 items, and .z items in Categories 3, 4, and 5, except for destinations in Country Groups D:5 countries.

obligations.summary: Exports, reexports or transfers under General or Data Center VEU are limited to validated end-users listed in supplement no. 7 to part 748; other end-users may not receive eligible items under these authorizations.

evidence.quote: The only end-users to whom eligible items may be exported, reexported, or transferred under a General VEU Authorization

obligations.summary: Requests for VEU authorization must be made as an advisory opinion request under 748.3(c), list the items by ECCN, and include the information in supplement no. 8; requests may come from exporters, reexporters or end-users.

evidence.quote: requests for authorization must be submitted in the form of an advisory opinion request

obligations.summary: In evaluating an end user for VEU eligibility, the End-User Review Committee considers a range of listed factors, including compliance record, need for on-site review, technology control plan and relationships with U.S. and foreign companies.

evidence.quote: In evaluating an end user for eligibility under authorization VEU, the ERC will consider a range of information

obligations.summary: Information submitted in a VEU request is treated as continuing representations; any material or substantive change relating to the authorization must be promptly reported to BIS, whether or not authorization has been granted.

evidence.quote: Any material or substantive change relating to the authorization must be promptly reported to BIS

obligations.summary: Items controlled under the EAR for missile technology (MT) and crime control (CC) reasons may not be exported or reexported under General or Data Center VEU Authorizations.

evidence.quote: Items controlled under the EAR for missile technology (MT) and crime control (CC) reasons may not be exported or reexported under General or Data Center VEU Authorizations.

obligations.summary: Before an initial export or reexport to a validated end-user under either VEU authorization, exporters or reexporters must obtain certifications from the end-user regarding end use and compliance with VEU requirements, containing the contents set out in supplement no. 8.

evidence.quote: exporters or reexporters must obtain certifications

obligations.summary: Certifications and all records relating to VEU must be retained under the recordkeeping requirements of part 762 of the EAR.

evidence.quote: Certifications and all records relating to VEU must be retained by exporters or reexporters

obligations.summary: Reexporters using General VEU Authorization must file annual reports to BIS; reexporters using Data Center VEU Authorization must file semi-annual reports. Each report lists, per validated end-user, name and address, eligible destination, quantity, value and ECCNs.

evidence.quote: Reexporters who make use of General VEU Authorizations are required to submit annual reports to BIS.

obligations.summary: End users under Data Center VEU must submit semi-annual reports to BIS covering current inventory of eligible items, dates and recipients of receipt, description of current compute use, and a list of current customers with their utilization.

evidence.quote: End users who make use of Data Center VEU Authorizations must submit reports to BIS semi-annually.

obligations.summary: On BIS request, exporters, reexporters, transferors and validated end-users must allow review of records, including on-site reviews of the information covered by paragraphs (e) and (f)(1).

evidence.quote: Upon request by BIS, exporters, reexporters, transferors, and validated end-users must allow review of records

obligations.summary: Exporters and reexporters shipping under either VEU authorization, and persons transferring in-country under General VEU, must give the receiving VEU written notice of the shipment or transfer listing VEU-authorized contents and ECCNs; notice timing is agreed in advance and the notices must be kept.

evidence.quote: are required to provide the VEUs to which they are shipping or transferring notice of the shipment or transfer

obligations.summary: A Data Center VEU application must describe physical and logical security requirements for each location housing controlled items, access policies, an information security plan (cybersecurity, logging and monitoring, technology control, personnel security, incident reporting), and a supply chain plan preventing PRC-origin equipment and PRC vendors in the data center environment.

evidence.provision: Supplement No. 8 to part 748, Part B(4)
evidence.quote: Describe physical and logical security requirements for each location the controlled items will be housed

obligations.summary: The application must include a signed statement on letterhead by a person authorized to bind the applicant, certifying compliance with VEU requirements, acknowledging end-use and diversion restrictions and recordkeeping, and agreeing to on-site reviews by U.S. Government officials.

evidence.provision: Supplement No. 8 to part 748, Part A(7)
evidence.quote: Include an original statement on letterhead

obligations.summary: If the End-User Review Committee approves a request, BIS issues a response letter granting VEU status.
obligations.conditional_on: If the End-User Review Committee approves the request

evidence.quote: BIS will issue a response in the form of a letter granting VEU status.

obligations.summary: The BIS approval letter states permitted items and any conditions required of the VEU; example conditions include physical and logical security requirements, prohibiting access by individuals or entities of concern, onsite inspections, and not providing computing power above prohibited thresholds.

evidence.quote: The letter will state the items that are permitted for export or reexport to the VEU, along with any conditions required of the VEU.

enforcement.authority: Not named for this action in the text; VEU status is granted by the End-User Review Committee under § 748.15(a)(1)
enforcement.triggered_by: The text states that VEU authorization may be revised, suspended or revoked, entirely or in part, but gives no triggering conditions. Private right of action is not addressed.

evidence.quote: The VEU authorization is subject to revision, suspension, or revocation entirely or in part.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment in the operative Data Center VEU provisions. Eligibility is set by ECCN, item category, licence requirement and destination group (Country Groups D:5 excluded). The ERC conditions refer to 'computing power above prohibited thresholds' without quantifying them. Supplement No. 7 restates General VEU item limits (e.g., APP 12.0 weighted teraflops; 13 microns) that belong to pre-existing General VEU entries and were not coded.
